sections.html:
Charleston County faces the Atlantic and, counting water, is the largest county in South Carolina at 1,357.99 square miles. Roughly a third of that area, 440.01 square miles, is water. Four counties share its borders: Berkeley, Georgetown, Colleton and Dorchester. The city of Charleston serves as the seat.

Residents numbered 408,235 in 2020, a gain of 16.6 percent over the 350,209 of 2010. The big population centers are Charleston city, North Charleston, Mount Pleasant and Summerville, while Isle of Palms, Folly Beach, Kiawah Island, Seabrook Island and Sullivan's Island make up the beach towns. Tiny places like Hollywood, Ravenel, Awendaw, McClellanville and Lincolnville still send their tax questions to the same county offices.

Your municipality matters. Cities and towns add their own levy to the county's, so neighbors with similar houses can open very different bills.

sections.h2: Where to pay and who to call
sections.html:
Property tax payments land at the Treasurer's counter in the O.T. Wallace County Office Building, 101 Meeting Street, Suite 120, Charleston 29401. Call (843) 958-4360 with questions. The counter is open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. until 5:00 p.m.

By mail, make a check or money order out to the Charleston County Treasurer and send it to P.O. Box 878, Charleston, SC 29402-0878. The county's public access website accepts online payments and adds a surcharge for cards. You cannot pay part of a bill, since state law bars the Treasurer from accepting partial payments.

Addresses are not the Treasurer's department. The Assessor and the Auditor hold owner and property addresses, so changes go there. After you sell, double-check that the old bill is not still headed to your mailbox.

Tax on real estate comes due January 15 of the next year. Missing that date starts a three-step penalty ladder, and after March 17 the account is turned over to the Delinquent Tax Department.

DatePenalty stepRunning total
After January 153 percent3 percent
After February 17 percent10 percent
After March 175 percent15 percent, then delinquent

There is an installment option. The Treasurer runs an advance plan at no extra cost for owners who have no mortgage escrow and no earlier-year balance. You make five equal payments on the 15th of February, April, June, August and October. The remainder is mailed by November 15 and falls due by January 15.

The county mails receipts to the bill's address. To send one somewhere new, include a change-of-address form with the payment. Anyone paying online gets a confirmation on screen and by email.

All Charleston County property was reappraised in 2025, with notices going out in August. A 15 percent cap held down the growth in taxable value for most parcels. Exceptions may apply to homes that sold or transferred in 2024, to new additions and to substantially improved property. After a reassessment, state law requires cities to reset their rates to stay revenue neutral, and the Auditor supplies the rollback figure. Questions about the process go to the reassessment hotline at (843) 958-4144.

Challenges have three tiers. An objection is an informal review. A protest is a formal one. An appeal is heard by the Board of Assessment Appeals, and a loser at that stage has 30 days to ask the Administrative Law Court for a hearing. Since reassessment repeats on a five-year schedule, ask the Assessor when the next round is planned and how long the appeal window will stay open.

sections.h2: Exemptions that matter when you sell or buy
sections.html:
Sales raise three questions: whether the 4 percent legal residence rate is in place, whether a homestead exemption applies, and whether the ATI exemption can soften a transfer. Each one runs on its own deadline. The 4 percent form is typically due January 15, and you can get it as a PDF or file it online.

  • Homestead: removes the first $50,000 of a legal residence's fair market value. The owner must meet the age, disability or blindness test, have lived in South Carolina for a year, and have held title by December 31 of the prior year.
  • ATI exemption: shields up to 25 percent of the value created by an assessable transfer. The property needs 6 percent taxation before and after, a value increase caused by the transfer, and a spot on the roll in the sale year. File on or before January 30 of the tax year you are requesting.

Call the Homestead Representative at (843) 958-4220 for the first, and the Assessor for the others. A sale is itself an assessable transfer that resets the next owner's value, although certain family and affiliated transfers are carved out.

sections.h2: Selling a Charleston County house with tax owed
sections.html:
A balance at closing is not a dead end. Your closing agent can pay it from the sale proceeds, so you avoid the full 15 percent penalty and the risk that the house is auctioned.

An auction can still be undone. After a delinquent sale, the owner, a mortgage creditor or a judgment creditor may redeem during the next twelve months by paying the taxes, penalties and costs, along with interest that steps from 3 percent up to 12 percent.

  1. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff before you accept an offer.
  2. Find out from the Assessor if your legal residence rate is on file.
  3. Send the Assessor and Auditor your current mailing address.

Cash Home Buyers buys Charleston County houses in any condition, from the city of Charleston out to Ladson, including homes with deferred repairs, tenants or probate. Send the address and your latest tax notice, and you will get an honest read on your options.

sections.h2: What to have ready for a sale
sections.html:
Gather the current tax bill, the notice from the 2025 reassessment, and proof that your legal residence application was filed. See whether the 15 percent cap applied to your parcel, since a buyer's first bill can look quite different once the transfer is assessed. If you ever paid at 6 percent while qualified for 4 percent, the Assessor can tell you what correction is available.

Hold on to the Treasurer's last receipt as well. It shows the address the county has on record, which is a quick way to spot an outdated mailing address before closing day.

Homestead is separate from the 4 percent rate, so a qualifying owner should confirm that both are on the account. Finally, ask your title company what it needs from the county. Most want a recent payoff, and they will also confirm whether any exemption on the property changes hands with the sale or ends with it.

faqs.q: When are Charleston County, SC property taxes due?
faqs.a: January 15 of the following year. A 3 percent penalty follows, rising to 10 percent in total after February 1 and 15 percent in total after March 17.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Charleston County property tax?
faqs.a: At the Treasurer's office, 101 Meeting Street, Suite 120, Charleston, or by mail to P.O. Box 878, Charleston, SC 29402-0878. Payment online is possible too. The phone is (843) 958-4360.

faqs.q: Can I pay Charleston County property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, if your account is not escrowed and has no unpaid earlier years. The advance installment plan has five advance payments and a balance due by January 15.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to apply for the 4 percent rate in Charleston County?
faqs.a: The usual deadline is January 15 each year. You can print the application as a PDF or complete it online.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Charleston County house with unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The closing agent can settle the taxes and penalties from your proceeds. If a tax sale already took place, redemption stays open for twelve months.
